posts.subject: Frage zu Legion 7i und Legion 5(i) Pro - 2025 - OLED
posts.author: Eradi
posts.message_html:
Hello everyone,

I would like to inherit my current, loyal Lenovo Legion 5 Pro.

The following options have emerged for me:

- Lenovo Legion 5 Pro (AMD) Gen 10 (2025)

- Lenovo Legion 5i Pro (Intel) Gen 10 (2025)

- Lenovo Legion 7i (Intel) Gen 10 (2025)

Now to my questions:

1) According to PSREF, the Legion 5 Pro and the Legion 5i Pro are also available with an IPS screen. I have been monitoring the Lenovo website for several weeks, and this variant does not seem to be available or configurable. Is there a way to specify a timeframe for availability?

2) In case I have to buy an OLED after all, I found out that the Lenovo Space app has some options to avoid OLED burn-in. Would an OLED burn-in be covered under one of the following manufacturer warranties?

a) Depot Warranty

b) Premium Care Onsite Support

c) Premium Care Plus

d) Lenovo Accidental Damage Protection

e) Lenovo Accidental Damage Protection One

Unfortunately, there are various statements on the internet, as well as through the Lenovo chat function. A definitive answer on whether OLED burn-in is covered or can be covered would be desirable and crucial for the purchasing decision. Ideally, an official Lenovo document on this would be made available. The warranty location can be assumed to be EU/Germany.

Best regards, Marcel

posts.author: Hector_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hi Marcel!

Thank you for reaching out to the Lenovo Community and sorry for the delayed response. I appreciate your patience and detailed inquiry regarding the Lenovo Legion 5 Pro, Legion 5i Pro, and Legion 7i models.

The IPS screen variants for the Legion 5 Pro and Legion 5i Pro are indeed listed in the PSREF. However, availability can vary based on region and stock levels. Unfortunately, I cannot provide a specific timeframe for when these models will be available on the Lenovo website. I recommend regularly checking the Official Shop Site. Additionally, you may contact Lenovo Sales directly for more precise information regarding stock and availability or reach out to our authorized retail partners in Germany here.

These warranty options you listed are repair services except for the ADP and ADP One which are considered add-ons. Some repair services such as the Premium Care Plus may already have ADP included unlike the others; otherwise, it needs to be purchased separately. ADP One is the limited version of the ADP since it only covers one repair of accidental damage during the term.

OLED Burn-in rarely happens unless there is a certain level of misuse; otherwise, it is covered by the warranty within normal usage. In situations where damage occurs accidentally or due to environmental factors, ADP is recommended to cover. For more info, you can check this link regarding Lenovo Service Agreements.

If you need further assistance or have additional questions, please feel free to reach out.

Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

topic_info.subject: Frage zu Legion 7i und Legion 5(i) Pro - 2025 - OLED
topic_info.message:
Hallo zusammen,

ich möchte mein aktuelles, treues, Lenovo Legion 5 Pro beerben.

Als Optionen für mich haben sich folgende Varianten ergeben:

- Lenovo Legion 5 Pro (AMD) Gen 10 (2025)

- Lenovo Legion 5i Pro (Intel) Gen 10 (2025)

- Lenovo Legion 7i (Intel) Gen 10  (2025)

Nun zu meinen Fragen:

1) Das Legion 5 Pro und das Legion 5i Pro, gibt es laut PSREF auch mit einem IPS Screen, ich beobachte die Lenovo-Seite seit mehreren Wochen, diese Variante scheint nicht verfügbar oder konfigurierbar zu sein, gibt es eine Möglichkeit hier einen Verfügbarkeitszeitraum zu benennen?

2) Für den Fall dass ich doch OLED kaufen müsste, habe ich heraus gefunden, dass die Lenovo Space App über einige Optionen verfügt OLED Burn in zu vermeiden. Wäre ein OLED Burn in im Rahmen einer der folgenden Herstellergarantien abgedeckt?

 a) Depot-Garantie

 b) Premium Care Onsite Support

 c) Premium Care Plus

d) Lenovo Accidential Damage Protection

e) Lenovo Accidential Damage Protection One

Leider gibt es im Internet verschiedene Aussagen, ebenso über die Lenovo Chatfunktion. Eine verbindliche Antwort, ob OLED Burn in abgedeckt ist oder abgedeckt werden kann wäre wünschenswert und für die Kaufentscheidung maßgeblich. Im Optimalfall wird ein offizielles Lenovo Dokument hierzu zur Verfügung gestellt. Als Garantieort kann EU/Deutschland angenommen werden.

Freundliche Grüße Marcel
